definition: Describing features or functionality that are available immediately upon installation without requiring additional configuration.
extendedDefinition: Out of the box describes product functionality that works immediately after installation, without scripting, configuration, or integration work. It is a measure of time-to-value and implementation risk: the more a product delivers out of the box, the faster teams achieve results and the fewer resources are consumed on setup. Buyers comparing products should distinguish out-of-the-box capability from potential once customized, since marketing materials emphasize the former while real-world deployments involve the latter. Typical questions include whether default workflows match the organization's process, whether standard reports answer the questions leaders actually ask, and whether integrations with existing systems exist today rather than on a roadmap. A strong out-of-the-box experience reduces dependency on consultants and accelerates adoption, which is why it is a top criterion for teams with limited implementation budgets.
